answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a jade as the anchor of the cost.
